summary: The settled way to hand a three-dimensional model from one tool to another. Everything about the shape of a thing and how its surface looks is finished, ratified and in the core: meshes, textures, a physically based material model, animation curves, skinning, morph targets, cameras, metres and a fixed axis convention. Everything about how a thing behaves is not. The whole specification text contains the word physics once, as a made-up name in an example, and the word audio zero times. Extensions carry the rest, so the level here follows a rule: native means the ratified core text, via-extension means a named extension the Khronos board has actually ratified, and partial means a named extension whose draft text is public but which is not ratified. Twenty-three extensions are ratified. Physics, audio and interactivity are not among them. One trap for a standards audience: this format has skins and joints but no agreed bone names, so an animation authored for one avatar will not play on another without a convention this specification does not supply.

coverage.note: This is the whole purpose of the format: a single file, plain text or binary, that carries a model between a creation tool and a runtime.

coverage.note: glTF is a transmission format for models and scenes. It says what to draw; how a runtime mixes that drawing with a live camera view of the room is the runtime's own presentation and no glTF property touches it.
A face and body stream comes off a device's sensors at run time. glTF carries no input model at all, and the face data it can hold is a stored morph target, which is scene.morph.

A scene format is exactly the kind of thing that could carry walkable surface, bounds and spawn points, and glTF carries none. The core specification has meshes, nodes, cameras, skins and animations, and no ratified Khronos extension in the registry declares navigable space or an arrival point. Whoever opens the file works it out again.

coverage.note: glTF publishes no units of logic to name. It registers extension name prefixes so two vendors cannot collide on a property name, which is a naming rule for the format, not an address for code somebody else can depend on.

No finished content passes through Khronos on its way to an audience. glTF is a file format, so there is no place in it where a review could stand, and it carries no field saying what review an asset has had.
glTF has no geographic frame of any kind, so it can neither declare a map of a place nor publish a transform between two maps. It is placed in the world by whatever loads it.
A glTF file is content, not a service bound to a place, and it declares no geographic area it applies to. Its bounds are in its own local axes.
The core extensionsUsed and extensionsRequired declarations identify additions and distinguish optional support from additions required to load an asset.
